"I'd make a retro-style Formula One career game with 8–12 teams, each having two drivers, where you create your own driver but don't get to choose your starting team. Instead, teams evaluate you and offer you a contract, ideally starting you at the bottom of the championship. Every driver has individual attributes rated 1–100, including pace, qualifying, aggression, overtaking, defending, consistency, wet-weather ability, tire management and mistake probability. Every car also has its own attributes, including top speed, acceleration, cornering, stability, oversteer, understeer, braking, reliability and tire wear. Driver ability and car performance should be completely independent, meaning a world-class driver could be stuck in a terrible car, while an average driver could find themselves in a championship-winning car. Throughout your career, you improve through experience, outperform teammates, build your reputation and receive offers from increasingly competitive teams. Drivers should also develop, decline with age and eventually retire, with new drivers entering the championship. Racing itself should include tire degradation, fuel weight, dirty air, collision damage, mechanical failures and dynamic weather, but without becoming overly complicated. The goal is to create an unpredictable championship where driver skill, car performance and team competitiveness all matter, and where building a successful career from the bottom is just as satisfying as winning championships. Visually, I'd want a simple retro aesthetic inspired by early PS2 and late PS1 racing games. Nothing overly realistic or graphically demanding. The cars should have recognizable shapes, basic but distinct liveries, simple lighting and slightly blocky models. Tracks should be colourful and recognizable, with relatively simple environments, grandstands, barriers and scenery. I'd prefer a clean third-person camera behind the car, with an optional cockpit view. The menus should be minimalistic, with simple typography, driver portraits, team logos, championship standings and basic statistics. The HUD should display speed, gear, lap times, position and tire condition without cluttering the screen. Overall, I want something that looks like a classic early 2000s Formula One game, with a slightly dated but charming presentation. The focus should be on the racing and career mode rather than impressive graphics.

---

"

## Objective
- Complete a playable retro-style Formula One career game in the existing project, with team contracts, driver development, championship progression, and accessible racing gameplay.

## Requirements
- Include 8–12 teams with two drivers each; create a driver without choosing a starting team, then receive team offers.
- Keep driver and car attributes separate; support development, teammate rivalry, reputation, contracts, aging, retirement, and new drivers.
- Include tire wear, fuel weight, dirty air, collision damage, mechanical failures, and dynamic weather without excessive complexity.
- Provide colorful late-PS1/early-PS2-inspired visuals, recognizable cars and tracks, third-person and optional cockpit views, clean HUD, standings, stats, minimal menus, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Build without clarification and note assumptions briefly at completion.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained browser game in `index.html`, with inline CSS and JavaScript.
- Championship is set up for 10 teams, 20 drivers, and a 12-track season, with canvas-based pseudo-3D racing.

## Work State
### Completed
- Rebuilt the missing application flow in `index.html`: driver creation, team offers, career dashboard, calendar and standings modals, development, racing, results, season progression, and localStorage persistence.
- Added team signing while maintaining 20 active drivers, plus contract offers at season end, driver aging, and occasional replacement drivers.
- Added canvas racing with chase/cockpit views, keyboard-intended and touch controls, weather, tire wear, fuel consumption, off-track behavior, collision damage, scoring, and race debrief.
- Verified JavaScript syntax with `node --check /tmp/opencode/check.js` and loaded the page with headless Chromium.

### Active
- Validate complete browser interactions and correct any gameplay defects.
- Implement or assess remaining requested mechanics: fuel weight, dirty air, and mechanical failures.

### Blocked
- Keyboard race input currently appears unbound: the race renderer reads `raceData.keys`, but no keyboard event listeners were added.
- Browser validation so far only confirmed page loading; no end-to-end race or career flow was exercised.

## Next Move
1. Add and test keyboard listeners for arrows, space, and `C` view toggle, including cleanup and pause behavior.
2. Run an end-to-end browser check for driver creation, team signing, race controls/results, season progression/contracts, save/load, and mobile layout.
3. Add lightweight fuel-weight, dirty-air, and mechanical-failure gameplay effects, or note any scoped simplifications at completion.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation; current changes are uncommitted.

## Important Context
- The original file was incomplete and ended after `careerPage()`; the game logic and closing HTML have since been rebuilt.
- Work remains uncommitted.

## Objective
- Complete a playable retro-style Formula One career game in the existing project, with team contracts, driver development, championship progression, and accessible racing gameplay.

## Requirements
- Include 8–12 teams with two drivers each; create a driver without choosing a starting team, then receive team offers.
- Keep driver and car attributes separate; support development, teammate rivalry, reputation, contracts, aging, retirement, and new drivers.
- Include tire wear, fuel weight, dirty air, collision damage, mechanical failures, and dynamic weather without excessive complexity.
- Provide colorful late-PS1/early-PS2-inspired visuals, recognizable cars and tracks, third-person and optional cockpit views, clean HUD, standings, stats, minimal menus, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Build without clarification and note assumptions briefly at completion.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained browser game in `index.html`, with inline CSS and JavaScript.
- Championship setup: 10 teams, 20 drivers, and a 12-track season, with canvas-based pseudo-3D racing.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented driver creation, starting team offers, career dashboard, calendar and standings modals, development, racing, results, season progression, contract offers, aging/replacement drivers, and localStorage persistence.
- Added keyboard controls for arrows, space, and `C` view toggle; pause/blur handling, input cleanup, and mobile touch controls.
- Added lightweight fuel-weight effect, simulated rival positions and dirty-air effects, and probabilistic mechanical issues/failures.
- Verified JavaScript syntax with `node --check /tmp/opencode/check.js`, loaded the page with headless Chromium, and exercised driver creation → signing → race input/view toggle → result save via CDP.

### Active
- Review gameplay balance and remaining mechanics against requested scope; make any final corrections.
- Confirm mobile layout and season-end progression/contracts through browser interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test longer race completion, collision/weather/failure effects, pause/resume, and season-end contract transitions.
2. Check mobile layout and persistence after reload; address any defects.
3. Summarize assumptions and remaining simplifications at completion.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation; current changes are uncommitted.

## Important Context
- The original file was incomplete and ended after `careerPage()`; the game logic and closing HTML have since been rebuilt.
- CDP smoke test passed: created “Test Driver,” signed a team, confirmed 20 drivers, observed keyboard acceleration and cockpit toggle, and reached a saved race classification.
- Race uses an approximate canvas pseudo-3D view and abstracted rival/race simulation rather than full physical simulation.

## Objective
- Complete the existing retro-style Formula One career game as a playable **mobile/phone game**, with career progression and accessible racing gameplay.

## Requirements
- Design for phones first, including usable touch controls and responsive layouts.
- Include 8–12 teams with two drivers each; create a driver without choosing a starting team, then receive offers.
- Support driver development, separate driver/car attributes, rivalry, reputation, contracts, aging, retirement, and new drivers.
- Include tire wear, fuel weight, dirty air, collision damage, mechanical failures, and dynamic weather without excessive complexity.
- Use colorful late-PS1/early-PS2-inspired visuals, recognizable cars and tracks, third-person and optional cockpit views, clean HUD, standings, stats, and minimal menus.
- Build without clarification and briefly note assumptions at completion.

## Decisions
- Implement as a self-contained browser game in `index.html`, with inline CSS and JavaScript.
- Use a 10-team, 20-driver championship with a 12-track season and canvas-based pseudo-3D racing.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented driver creation, starting team offers, career dashboard, calendar and standings modals, driver development, racing, results, season progression, contract offers, aging/replacement drivers, and localStorage persistence.
- Added keyboard and touch controls, chase/cockpit toggle, pause and automatic blur/visibility pause, and race-control cleanup.
- Added fuel-weight effects, simulated rival positions and dirty-air effects, and probabilistic mechanical issues/failures.
- Prior CDP smoke test passed driver creation, signing, race input, view toggle, and result saving.

### Active
- Recenter review and testing around the phone-first requirement; verify mobile layout, touch-control usability, and save persistence after reload.
- Test full race completion, pause/resume, fuel behavior, and season-end contract transitions.
- Make final corrections and summarize assumptions and remaining simplifications.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Inspect and test the game at phone-sized viewports, especially race HUD/control overlap, touch input behavior, and safe-area/layout issues.
2. Run full-race and career progression tests, including pause/resume, persistence after reload, and season-end contracts.
3. Fix issues found, then summarize assumptions and remaining simplifications.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation; currently uncommitted.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- The user emphasized: “this is meant to be a mobile / phone game”.
- Existing CSS shows touch controls only at widths up to 850px, while the race HUD and controls need phone-specific verification.
- Racing uses an approximate canvas pseudo-3D view and abstracted rival/race simulation rather than full physical simulation.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete `index.html` as a playable, phone-first retro Formula One career game, then verify its mobile controls and career progression.

## Requirements
- Design for phones first, including usable touch controls and responsive layouts.
- Include 8–12 teams with two drivers each; create a driver without choosing a starting team, then receive offers.
- Support driver development, separate driver/car attributes, rivalry, reputation, contracts, aging, retirement, and new drivers.
- Include tire wear, fuel weight, dirty air, collision damage, mechanical failures, and dynamic weather without excessive complexity.
- Use colorful late-PS1/early-PS2-inspired visuals, recognizable cars and tracks, third-person and optional cockpit views, clean HUD, standings, stats, and minimal menus.
- Build without clarification and briefly note assumptions at completion.

## Decisions
- Implement as a self-contained browser game in `index.html`, with inline CSS and JavaScript.
- Use a 10-team, 20-driver championship with a 12-track season and canvas-based pseudo-3D racing.
- Keep the simulation lightweight and phone-friendly, with simplified race logic and localStorage persistence.

## Work State
